Maine Senate Confirms Vaughan Woodruff as Chair of the State Workforce Development Board

October 5, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Senate confirmed Vaughan Woodruff, principal of EquinoxDG, to a second term as chair of the State Workforce Development Board (SWDB). Gov. Janet Mills announced her nomination of Woodruff on Sept. 8, 2026. Woodruff has served as chair of the SWDB since 2023.

Prior to founding EquinoxDG, Woodruff was vice president of regulatory reform at the Interstate Renewable Energy Council and vice president of workforce development and interconnection strategy at ReVision Energy, where he oversaw the company's long-term strategic vision for training and talent development and developed nationally recognized registered apprenticeships in clean energy.

"The State Workforce Development Board plays a critical role in coordinating Maine's workforce development efforts to support economic growth and address workforce challenges," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "Vaughan Woodruff is a well-respected business leader with deep workforce expertise. His continued leadership will help maintain momentum as we strengthen Maine's workforce and economy."

"I appreciate the trust that Gov. Mills and the Maine Senate have placed in me through my nomination and confirmation to continue serving the people of Maine in this role," said Woodruff. "I feel privileged to work with the outstanding staff and members of the Board to increase the accessibility of the workforce system to Maine workers and businesses and to proactively address the workforce challenges ahead of us."

Woodruff is a seventh-generation Maine native who was raised in Pittsfield. He earned a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from the University of Maine and a master's degree in education from Prescott College in Arizona. Woodruff was the founder and CEO of Insource Renewables, an employee-owned solar company that was recognized as a Best for the World for Workers company by B Lab prior to its acquisition by ReVision Energy in 2021.

During Woodruff's tenure as chair, the SWDB has:

  • Launched Work Source Maine, the state's online resource connecting job seekers, students, parents, educators, career counselors and employers with resources to explore, plan and achieve career and workforce goals;

  • Launched the Maine Workforce Pell program, which expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term, career-focused training programs that deliver industry-recognized credentials and measurable employment results, preparing students for in-demand occupations; and

  • Secured $15M+ in funding to support industry partnerships in advanced manufacturing, forest bioproducts and defense, and expand career exploration, job supports, and upskilling investments including registered pre-apprenticeships

As chair, Woodruff will continue to work with the SWDB, state agencies, education and training providers, employers and other partners to strengthen Maine's workforce development system and help connect Maine people with career opportunities.

Woodruff serves on the Electrical Technologies Advisory Committee at Kennebec Valley Community College and previously served on the Western Mountains Committee of the Maine Community Foundation and the Pittsfield Planning Board. Woodruff lives in Pittsfield with his wife, Holly Zadra, and their two sons, Eamon and Goran.

October 6, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Board of Occupational Safety and Health (BOSH) and the Maine Department of Labor Bureau of Labor Standards (BLS) Workplace Safety and Health Division invite interested parties and the public to participate in listening sessions on a proposed voluntary compliance directive on indoor air quality.

BOSH regulates and enforces workplace safety and health rules that apply to public employers, including state and local governmental agencies, school districts and quasi-governmental agencies. BOSH is considering publishing a voluntary compliance directive to help public employers monitor and maintain healthy indoor air quality in public workplaces. The proposed compliance directive is based in part on the research and recommendations of the Indoor Air Quality Advisory Group in 2025.

item.title: US Department of Labor cites Pennsylvania excavation employer for failing to provide trench protection following fatal trench cave-in
item.description: CHAMBERSBURG, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an excavation contractor for willful and serious safety violations after a young worker was fatally injured in a trench collapse. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an investigation into Jonas David Wagoner – doing business as J.D. Wagoner Excavating – on April 2, 2026, and found workers were installing a storm sewer system 12 feet below ground level in a trench that was not adequately protected from soil collapse. When a portion of the trench's wall failed, the unrestrained soil engulfed one worker. The agency issued a willful violation for failure to protect workers from cave-ins and two repeat violations for failing to assign a competent person to conduct daily trench inspections and removing employees from hazardous conditions.In addition, the employer received three serious violations for failure to provide construction hazard prevention training to employees, establish a safe means for workers to exit the excavation site, keep materials at least two feet from the edge of an excavation site, and restrain side materials from becoming roll-in hazards. OSHA proposed $254,884 in penalties. The employer has 15 business days from receiving receipt of its citations and penalties to request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

item.title: Weiss v. Maine Soapstone Co.
item.description:
STATE OF MAINE APPELLATE DIVISION WORKERS’ COMPENSATION BOARD Case No. App. Div. 26-0002 Decision No. 26-10
JEROME WEISS (Appellant)
v.
MAINE SOAPSTONE COMPANY , INC. (Appellee)
and
MAINE EMPLOYERS’ MUTUAL INSURANCE COMPANY (Insurer)
Decided: October 8, 2026 Conference held: September 2, 2026
PANEL MEMBERS: Administrative Law Judges Biddings, Chabot, and Rooks By: Administrative Law Judge Biddings [¶1] Jerome Weiss appeals from a decision of a Workers’ Compensation Board administrative law judge ( Smith, ALJ) denying his Petition to Reopen for Mistake of Fact or Fraud. Mr. Weiss contends that the ALJ erred in determining that his petition was untimely under 39-A M.R.S.A. § 321(2), and in concluding that even if the petition had been timely, Mr. Weiss did not establish that Maine Soapstone Company committed fraud. We disagree with Mr. Weiss’s contentions and affirm the decision.
2
I. BACKGROUND1 [¶2] Mr. Weiss sustained a work-related shoulder injury on February 3, 2009, while working for Maine Soapstone Company. Initially, Maine Soapstone voluntarily paid Mr. Weiss lost time and medical benefits. On September 13, 2010, Maine Soapstone issued a 21-day letter informing Mr. Weiss and the board of their intention to discontinue Mr. Weiss’s benefits as of October 5, 2010. See 39-A M.R.S.A. § 205(9). [¶3] In response to the discontinuance of his benefits, Mr. Weiss filed a Petition for Review , Request for Provisional Order , and a Petition for Award of Compensation regarding the February 3, 2009, date of injury. During the litigation, Mr. Weiss underwent an independent medical examination with Dr. Hall. See 39-A M.R.S.A. § 312. Dr. Hall opined that the effects of Mr. Weiss’s injury were ongoing and that he had retained a partial work capacity. An evidentiary hearing was held on May 16, 2011, before a board hearing officer (Pelletier, HO).2

item.title: Keith Sonderling sworn in as 31st US Secretary of Labor
item.description: WASHINGTON – Keith Sonderling was sworn in today as the 31st U.S. Secretary of Labor during a ceremony administered by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in the Oval Office. Sonderling has led the U.S. Department of Labor as Acting Secretary since April 2026. He previously served as Deputy Secretary of Labor after confirmation by the U.S. Senate in March 2025.President Donald J. Title IV PostsecondaryInstitutions: Workforce Pell Program Applications Open for Second Review Cycle Through Nov. 13

October 14, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist | media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA -The State Workforce Development Board(SWDB) is accepting applications from Title IV postsecondary institutionsseeking stateapproval to offer programs eligible for federal Workforce Pell Grants. Applications for the second review cycle are due Friday, Nov. 13

Maine's Workforce Pell application provides an online process for eligible postsecondary institutions to seek approval to offer short-term workforce training programs that meet federal Workforce Pell Grant requirements. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly by the SWDB.

Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage and in-demand careers. States are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before they are submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state,"said Vaughan Woodruff, chair of the State Workforce Development Board."The program's support for training that connects people with skills needed for Maine's workforce presents a significant opportunity for Maine workers and employers."

The Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy establishesthe state's process foridentifying, reviewing and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. The policy was developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System and University of MaineSystem.

"Workforce Pell brings a new source of federal funding to Maine's short-term workforce training programs," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "We are excited to help Maine's postsecondary institutions take advantage of this opportunity to strengthen their programs, reach more students and prepare Maine's workforce for the future."

The SWDB will evaluate applications and make recommendations to the Governor for state certification. Programs certified by the Governor will then be submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval. Following federal approval, the SWDB will publish the list of Maine-certified Workforce Pell programs on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage within 30 days.

Institutions can find the Workforce Pell application, eligibility requirements, program guidance and additional information on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage.

item.title: US Department of Labor announces field assistance bulletin withdrawing 3 opinion letters on tipped employees
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division today announced the issuance of a new field assistance bulletin addressing the treatment of related duties performed by tipped employees under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Field Assistance Bulletin No. 2026-1 brings the division’s guidance on tipped employees with dual jobs into alignment with current regulations.The bulletin withdraws the division’s 1979, 1980, and 1985 opinion letters concerning the application of dual jobs regulations to tipped employees. The withdrawal of the three opinion letters is necessary because they no longer reflect the division’s policy or interpretation of the FLSA. The bulletin also clarifies that the current dual jobs regulation focuses on whether an employee performs duties related to the employee’s tipped occupation, rather than imposing a specific percentage-based limit on the time an employee may spend performing related, non-tipped duties within that occupation.The publication of the new bulletin follows a 2024 federal court decision that vacated the department’s 2021 dual jobs final rule. After that decision, the department removed the regulatory text adopted under the 2021 rule and reinstated the original dual jobs regulations.The new field assistance bulletin clarifies that no current Wage and Hour Division guidance relies on the former percentage-based limit on the time a tipped employee may spend performing related, non-tipped duties, commonly known as the 80/20 rule. item.title: Consent judgment orders California-based home appliance company to pay $800K to 339 employees denied overtime pay
item.description: LOS ANGELES – The U.S. Department of Labor has obtained a consent judgment requiring a home appliance company to pay $800,000 in back wages and damages to 339 employees after an investigation found the company violated federal wage laws.The judgment comes after the department’s Wage and Hour Division investigated Coway USA Inc. and found that the employer paid employees on a piece-rate basis and failed to pay employees for time spent attending mandatory meetings, picking up and loading supplies, and performing work before and after their shifts, in violation of the Fair Labor Standards Act. Investigators also found that Coway did not include nondiscretionary incentives, bonuses, and commissions in overtime pay calculations and frequently reduced the number of hours employees recorded working on their timecards.Entered in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California on Sept. 9, the consent judgment requires Coway to record all hours the implicated employees worked, including time they spend picking up supplies, attending mandatory training, and communicating with customers before and after appointments. Coway is also required to give employees pay statements that show their hours worked, services provided to customers, and the rate Coway paid for the hours and services. The consent judgment orders Coway USA Inc. to pay $400,000 in unpaid overtime wages and an equal amount in damages to 339 employees working in the greater metro areas of Los Angeles, New York City, and Washington, D.C. The company also agreed to pay $10,000 in penalties for willful violations. Coway USA Inc. is a subsidiary of Coway Co. Ltd., a multinational company specializing in home appliances. The company installs and maintains various appliances, including water and air filtration products throughout the U.S.Employers and employees can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor announced today that its Mine Safety and Health Administration has awarded more than $10.5 million in grants to reduce mining accidents, injuries, and illnesses by supporting training and education programs.The agency is awarding these grants to support the delivery of federally mandated training for new and experienced miners at surface and underground coal and metal and nonmetal mines. item.title: US Department of Labor cites Illinois utility construction company for repeated exposure to trenching hazards
item.description: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Frankfort-based utility construction company for repeatedly exposing employees to excavation safety hazards after federal investigators observed employees working in an unprotected trench.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration initiated an investigation of Always Underground LLC as part of its National Emphasis Program on Trenching after witnessing employees working in an unprotected trench deeper than eight feet.OSHA cited the employer for three repeat violations for failing to provide workers with a safe means of egress, to install a trench protective system that would protect against cave-ins, and to keep excavated or other materials and equipment at least 2 feet from the edge. Additionally, the agency cited the employer for a serious violation for failing to provide workers with protective hardhats against falling objects.In total, OSHA proposed $380,664 in penalties.The employer has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.
